precepts.text: For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous. They didn't want that.
precepts.point: That verse speaks volumes. Deceivableness: the easy word is deceit. Unrighteousness: sin. All deceit of sin, breaking God's laws. In them that perish, because they received not the love of the truth: this is about our people.
precepts.why:
“For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.” The love of God is keeping his commandments, and they are not grievous. They didn't want that.

That is why the videos were shown. A pastor gets caught on video, and people come back for church services the next week. That's how fake you black people are: you'll see it with video proof and you'll still show up the next week. Same thing with Teddy Snakes after he got caught on video: I know you're waiting to hear me address these allegations, but I will not address them on the Lord's day. Everybody started screaming, and y'all still in the church. Y'all don't believe in God. Y'all care about the man instead of God's plan.

And that pastor and that woman got a $600,000 bond, while the Jake that killed that brother got $10,000. You can't make this up. Showing you the difference.

All of it comes back to this verse: “they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved.” They love the man and the church, not the love of God, which is to keep his commandments.

precepts.text: The record that God gave of his Son is the whole Bible, starting in the Old Testament. At the time these letters were written, much of the New Testament was not there yet; the record was the Old Testament. The manna, the cloud, the rock, the water that came out of it so they could live: it physically happened so that we could have that today. He that hath the Son hath life: that is the bread, the sustenance from heaven.
precepts.point: I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
“He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.” Christians stop and say this record is exclusively the New Testament. No. The record that God gave of his Son is the whole Bible, starting in the Old Testament.

At the time these letters were written, maybe they had the gospels at best, but a lot of the New Testament was not there. So where do you find the record God gave? In the Old Testament: the manna, the cloud, the rock, the water that came out of it so that they could live. It physically happened so that we could have that today.

“And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.” That is the daily bread, the daily nourishment. “He that hath the Son hath life”: that is the bread, the sustenance from heaven, the Holy Spirit. “and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.”

So it is not just, oh, I accept Christ, and that's all. It is everything we have read up to this point and everything in the Bible in its totality. That is the life Christ means when he says, I am the life.

precepts.text: Little children, keep yourselves from idols. Stay away from it.
precepts.point: Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led. Why does he bring this up before what he is about to go over? Because they were not accustomed to godly order or sound doctrine. They were following dumb idols, doing what those idols' customs wanted instead of what the most high God wanted. To try to teach organization to a Hellenized Jew is extremely difficult; you got to let them know, that is not us anymore, you got to renew your mind.
precepts.why:
Paul reminds the Corinthians where they came from: “Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led.” John gives the charge that goes with it: “Little children, keep yourselves from idols.” Stay the heck away from them. Stay away from it.

This was us. Esau's successful mission was to make our nation forget the laws of God and change the ordinances, to take away our heritage and make us become something we are not. They created that mind frame here, and you see it amongst our people.

Once you come into the truth you are supposed to go ten times harder and repent, not go back to the idols you were carried away to. Habakkuk showed where the idol worshipper ends up: destruction, speaking to wood and dumb stone that cannot teach.

So Paul clears away the old idol mindset before he teaches the diversities of gifts, administrations and operations in the one body. Keep yourselves from idols, renew your mind, and you can learn the godly order the Most High set in his body.

precepts.text: This is the love of God, that we keep his commandments, and his commandments are not grievous; the opposite of this is how you show him you hate him.
precepts.point: From the jump it has always been the same: love God, keep the commandments; nothing changed between the covenants.

note.label: Deuteronomy 7: A Holy People, Chosen Above All People

precepts.why:
“By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God, and keep his commandments. For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.”

This is the same teaching as Moses: the faithful God “keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations”. Loving the Most High is keeping his commandments. And the opposite of this is how you show him you hate him: refusing his commandments shows him with your actions that you hate him, and then judgment comes, for he “repayeth them that hate him to their face, to destroy them”.

From the jump it has always been the same: love God, keep the commandments. Nothing changed between the covenants; John and Moses say the same thing.

precepts.text: This is the confidence that we have in him: if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us, and we have the petitions that we desired of him.
precepts.point: Why did the Lord grant her petition? It was the will of the Most High for Samuel to come through Hannah; it was just in his time. And she was granted it because of what she did before she even asked: she kept his commandments and did those things that are pleasing in his sight.

note.label: 1 Samuel 1: Hannah's Vow and the Birth of Samuel

precepts.why:
“And this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us: And if we know that he hear us, whatsoever we ask, we know that we have the petitions that we desired of him.”

Hannah poured out her soul before the Lord, speaking in her heart so that only her lips moved, and Eli took her for drunken. When she told him, “I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the Lord”, Eli answered, “Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him.” She believed when she heard the word of Eli: she “went her way, and did eat, and her countenance was no more sad.”

Why did the Lord grant her petition? It was the will of the Most High for Samuel to come through Hannah; it was just in his time.

Understand this: a lot of us pray for things that the Lord has not given to us. The Most High has the infinite and ultimate wisdom and knows what is best for us, so some things he keeps back from us, and we have to accept that and know that. If it be his will, we receive what we ask, in his time; if it is not his will, we will not receive it.

precepts.text: All unrighteousness is sin; to be unrighteous is to not keep the commandments.
precepts.point: To be righteous is to observe to do all the commandments of the Lord; all unrighteousness is sin, and sin is the transgression of the law. David was righteous and did not want to war against his own son, yet good was repaid to him, while the sinner was pursued by his own evil.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

precepts.why:
“All unrighteousness is sin”. To be unrighteous is to not keep the commandments, and sin is the transgression of the law.

Ahithophel walked in unrighteousness, and his own evil pursued him to the end: he put his household in order, “and hanged himself, and died, and was buried in the sepulchre of his father.”

precepts.text: This is the confidence we have in him, that if we ask anything according to his will he hears us; ask according to his will, not to stumble somebody or to boast on social media, but to serve the nation.
precepts.point: Delight thyself in the Most High and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart; commit thy way unto him and he shall bring it to pass.

note.label: Psalm 37: Fret Not Because of Evildoers

precepts.why:
“Delight thyself also in the Lord; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart. Commit thy way unto the Lord; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass.” John gives the condition on those desires: “this is the confidence that we have in him, that, if we ask any thing according to his will, he heareth us”.

Ask according to his will: not to stumble somebody, not to boast on social media, but to serve the nation. When you delight yourself in the Most High by keeping the commandments and trusting him, he brings it to pass. If you are always doubting, or asking for stuff without believing in him, it is not going to happen. That is why we have to continually meditate in the word day and night.

precepts.text: This is the love of God, that we keep His commandments, and His commandments are not grievous.
precepts.point: The seed of His servants shall inherit it, and they that love His name shall dwell therein. Those that keep the commandments are going to dwell there.
precepts.why:
David closes the psalm with the promise: “For God will save Zion, and will build the cities of Judah: that they may dwell there, and have it in possession.” Only the oppressed need to be saved, and that is us. Then he says who will dwell there: “The seed also of his servants shall inherit it: and they that love his name shall dwell therein.”

John tells us what it means to love his name: “For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.” Loving the Most High is not a feeling; it is keeping his commandments, and they are not too heavy to bear.

So those that love his name in Psalm 69 are those that keep the commandments. They are the ones who are going to dwell in Zion when God saves it and builds the cities of Judah again.

precepts.text: All unrighteousness is sin, and there is a sin not unto death.
precepts.point: There is no sin in the Most High. Our people may struggle saying you cannot keep all the laws, but the Most High says His laws are not grievous and He did not give any man permission to sin.

note.label: Psalm 92: Planted in the House of the Lord

precepts.why:
The righteous bring forth fruit in old age “To shew that the Lord is upright: he is my rock, and there is no unrighteousness in him.” John tells what unrighteousness is: “All unrighteousness is sin: and there is a sin not unto death.”

All unrighteousness is sin, so there being no unrighteousness in the Most High means there is no sin in him. He is upright, and he is our rock. And there is a sin not unto death, so those planted in his house who stumble are not cut off; they still bring forth fruit and show that he is upright.

precepts.text: This is the love of God, that we keep His commandments, and His commandments are not grievous; that is how we love God.
precepts.point: He preserveth the souls of His saints and delivereth them out of the hand of the wicked.

note.label: Psalm 97: A Fire Goeth Before Him

precepts.why:
Ye that love the Lord, hate evil. How do we love the Lord? We cannot hug him. “For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.” We love God by keeping his commandments, and they are not grievous.

If you love God's commandments you hate sin, and if you keep his commandments you abstain from breaking his laws. That is what it means to love the Lord and hate evil.

precepts.text: This is the love of God, that we keep His commandments.
precepts.point: The Most High preserves all that love Him but destroys the wicked; loving Him means keeping His commandments.

note.label: Psalm 145: The Greatness and Mercy of the Most High

precepts.why: “The Lord preserveth all them that love him: but all the wicked will he destroy.” Loving him means keeping his commandments: “For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.” He fulfills the desire of them that fear him, hears their cry, and saves them, and those he preserves are those who love him by keeping his commandments.

precepts.text: The whole world lieth in wickedness, keeping none of the commandments, until the judgments come.
precepts.point: When His judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness, for right now the wicked are lofty and in high places; when Christ returns there will be no more celebrating Christmas and the other pagan holidays.

note.label: Isaiah 26: A Song of Salvation and the Straight Gate

precepts.why:
“for when thy judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness.” Right now they have not learned it. “And we know that we are of God, and the whole world lieth in wickedness.” The whole world lies in wickedness, keeping none of the commandments, until the judgments come.

Right now the wicked are lofty and in high places, while Israel waits in the way of His judgments and seeks Him early with soul and spirit. When Christ returns there will be no more celebrating Christmas and the other pagan holidays; then the inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness.

precepts.text: He that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.
precepts.point: He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
“He that hath received his testimony hath set to his seal that God is true.” John writes the other side of that in his epistle: “He that believeth on the Son of God hath the witness in himself: he that believeth not God hath made him a liar; because he believeth not the record that God gave of his Son.”

Not to receive his testimony is to call the record God gave of his son a lie. He that believes on the Son has the witness in himself, and has set to his seal that God is true; he that believes not has made God a liar. That is why “he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.”
